issue_context.title: Expose subquery resolution via Select() via interval or new hint
issue_context.body:
## Proposal

Currently, Thanos does push-down in some instances e.g. when the user's query has a function like `max()`. This means that the query itself is pushed down to the leaf node i.e. Prometheus itself executes that query. This helps speed up queries because all samples don't need to be sent to a central location for evaluation.

`step` parameter is used to detect whether there is a range query or not: https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/blob/main/pkg/store/prometheus.go#L249-L256. However, right now even subqueries set the `step` parameter to zero. I believe this is because the original `EvalStmt` has `Interval` set as zero https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/promql/engine.go#L630-L638 (take a look at `populateSeries` and `s.Interval == 0`). 

All of this means that Thanos right now incorrectly evaluates pushed-down queries with subqueries in them because it evaluates an instant query at the leaf node.

I suggest changing `Interval` in `populateSeries` accordingly if we are populating series for a subquery. Or perhaps there could be a separate SelectHint for this use case?
comments: I would invest in Prometheus hints to help us more. They are designed to provide information for more efficient results from underlying selects (:

review_comments: Should you not always try to get the subquery interval and set that if it is non-zero? Because that is what will be applied to the vector selector in that case. Can you try a query on Thanos with query interval and subquery interval are incompatible (i.e. not divisible by each other).
s.Interval will be 0 only in the case of an instant query I believe

Not sure if I understood the comment but with a range query, we want to pass the original interval, and in the case of an instant query with a subquery inside of it, we would like to somehow know about the interval of that subquery. So, my change here passes the interval of the inner-most subquery via the select hints in such a case. An alternative would be to have a separate field for the subquery interval. Instant queries can still be detected if `mint == maxt`?

If I got your question correctly then that is already handled by adjusting `mint` so that the results of the pushed down would fall on the expected timestamps [here](https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/blob/main/pkg/store/prometheus.go#L157-L174).

Even in case of a range query, the samples required for a subquery will be aligned with the subquery interval and not the range query interval (think of subquery as yet another range query with some timestamp alignments). So I meant literally only taking innermost subquery interval iff it exists. Was there any specific reason to prefer the range query interval if there was a subquery?
I did not know that. Let me update my branch.
